course.title: System Design for Working Engineers
course.subtitle: HLD and LLD you can defend
course.summary: Capacity estimation, service boundaries, storage choices and consistency trade-offs, taught as decisions with costs rather than as diagrams to memorise.
overview: System design gets taught as a gallery of reference architectures to reproduce on a whiteboard. That works until an interviewer, or a production incident, asks why.
This course treats design as a sequence of decisions, each with a cost and a set of conditions under which it is wrong. You will finish able to justify a design rather than recite one.
whatYouWillLearn: Turn a vague requirement into numbers you can design against
Estimate capacity, storage and bandwidth without hand waving
Choose between SQL and NoSQL based on access patterns
Design caching with an invalidation story that holds
Draw service boundaries along data ownership
Reason about CAP trade-offs in concrete terms
Plan a migration that can ship in phases and roll back

curriculum.title: Caching and CDNs
lessons: What is safe to cache and for how long
Cache keys and the dimensions that matter
Stampedes and how to avoid them

curriculum.title: Consistency and availability
lessons: Eventual consistency users can live with
Distributed transactions and why to avoid them

curriculum.title: Putting it together
lessons: Designing a feed or catalogue service

audience: Engineers with two or more years of experience preparing for senior interviews
Backend developers who are being asked to design rather than only implement
Anyone who has inherited a system and needs a framework for changing it safely
prerequisites: Experience building or maintaining a backend service
Working knowledge of databases and HTTP
